neighbours.label: watching, looking or checking actions in narrative (a character watches or inspects something)
fire: All afternoon the fisherman watched the clouds gather over the bay.
"Hold the torch," she whispered. "I'll check the lock on the back door."
From the porch the old woman watched the children race across the field.
The pilot leaned forward and looked at the gauges one more time.
Every night the guards watched the gate until the sun came up.
"Stay in the car," he said. "I'll look under the hood and see what's wrong."
The boy pressed his face to the glass and watched the snow fall on the street.
Before dawn the shepherd checked the fence for any gaps the wolves could use.
quiet: All afternoon the fisherman mended nets by the edge of the bay.
"Hold the torch," she whispered. "We need to leave by the back door."
From the porch the old woman called the children in for supper.
The pilot leaned forward and spoke quietly into the radio.
Every night the guards locked the gate and went to bed early.
"Stay in the car," he said. "I'll walk to the garage and get some help."
The boy pulled on his boots and ran out into the snowy street.
Before dawn the shepherd led the flock down to the lower pasture.
